assignments.name: Presentation
assignments.directions: Mental Health Presentation In this activity, you will use what you have learned from the lectures and readings regarding mental health disorders to create a presentation. Select one mental health disorder you have studied in this unit. Possible topics include depression, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, or personality disorders. Create a PowerPoint presentation. Your presentation should include the following: Title slide-containing your name, class period, teacher, and date Four to five informational slides-containing the name of the disorder, the classification (type) of disorder, facts, symptoms, and characteristics of the disorder. Describe possible treatments, help, and resources available. Include research on the racial and socioeconomical disparities for treatment facilities/access to doctors and medication. Include ways to help defeat any stigmas associated with this disorder, and why people with this disorder need to be treated with respect and dignity. Add images, charts, graphs, or designs to enhance your presentation. Conclusion slide-containing a summary of the information. Make sure to cite sources for any resources or images used in your presentation. Be sure to use reliable resources with valid health information.

announcements.name: Student Forum Membership and 1st Meeting Information
announcements.directions: Hey Vaqueros! Are you looking for a way to get involved on campus, gain a leadership position, and leadership credit? Student Forum is a great opportunity to gain leadership experience, which can be difficult for students across all grade levels to come across. As a Student Forum member, there are many opportunities for greater involvement and leadership positions. By joining, you are a TA Representative, helping to spread Student Forum’s message of inclusivity by making announcements to your TA. Members are also provided the opportunity to share their voice on campus issues to make large-scale change on campus! We will be having our first meeting at lunch in HLG this Wednesday (9/23), so be sure to come to learn more about Student Forum, how to get nationally recognized leadership credits, and get more involved in on campus leadership. We will also be answering any questions you may have asked on the Google Form in this meeting. Student Forum is a great place to begin your involvement within student leadership and accepts anyone willing to join. Students that complete the point requirement will receive nationally recognized leadership credit that will be placed on their transcript. Please fill out the interest form below to become a Student Forum Member today. Join our email list with this link: https://forms.gle/K8fxCYy8Fs6uCTNU8

announcements.name: Science Fair Sign-Ups for 6th Grade (K-8 Schools), Middle and High Schools due on Oct 2nd!
announcements.directions: Hi all, This is a friendly reminder that if you are hoping to compete in the IUSD Science Fair for secondary schools, the due date to sign-up is next Friday, October 2, 2026. This is a strict deadline. Please see the forms below: Middle School and 6th Grade (K-8 Schools only) Form High School Form Looking ahead, your next upcoming deadline following the sign-up is Friday, 10/16, where you need to schedule an office hours with your science teacher advisor. What you need to show them: Your project proposal in a slideshow Any certification forms already completed if applicable If you need to complete certification forms, you must also register for OCSEF by Mon, 11/2. OCSEF will then email your teacher advisor to get their signature. Once you receive confirmation that OCSEF has approved your project, you may begin. If you do not need certification forms, your teacher can let you know when it's safe to begin your project. Check out the Canvas modules for more support and resources. Please reach out to your science teacher or site coordinator for any further questions! :-)
